paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea: your life runs on seasons, and God is not surprised by a single one. The Teacher says, "To everything there is a season, and a time for every purpose under heaven" (Ecclesiastes 3:1). Weeping, laughing, keeping, discarding, silence, speaking, all of it has its time (Ecclesiastes 3:4, 6, 7). So when you land in a hard season, you haven't fallen out of the plan.

Now look at what the Teacher says about God's hand in all of this. "He has made everything beautiful in its time. He has also set eternity in the hearts of men, yet they cannot fathom the work that God has done from beginning to end" (Ecclesiastes 3:11). That means a baker will feel a longing for FOREVER and still not see the whole picture. I think that's okay, friend. You don't have to see the whole batch to trust the One running the oven.

So what do you do while you wait? The Teacher says, "I know that there is nothing better for them than to rejoice and do good while they live," and that eating, drinking and finding satisfaction in your labor is "the gift of God" (Ecclesiastes 3:12-13). Everything God does "endures forever; nothing can be added to it or taken from it" (Ecclesiastes 3:14). So rejoice, do good, and enjoy the work in front of you today, because what God builds will last.
